# What should you write in a gratitude journal at night when the day went badly?

The App Store description for our app opens with a scene we hear often: lying in bed replaying everything that went wrong today. We build Thankful, a gratitude journal for iPhone and iPad, and that night-time moment is exactly what it is designed for — three small writing spaces, a daily affirmation, a calendar history of what you already saved, and a streak that shows the days you returned. This guide is our first-hand account of how to use those three spaces on a bad day, without pretending the day was good, what the app costs, and what our measured App Store numbers look like so far.

You do not need to turn a hard day into a lesson. On a bad day, a gratitude entry is not a verdict on the day. It is a record of one or two specific things that were also true.

## Why is writing harder on a bad day?

A blank page asks for a summary, and a bad day already feels too large to summarise. Two other problems get in the way. The first is honesty: writing something cheerful can feel false, so you write nothing. The second is size: a full journal page asks for more than the last minutes of the day can give.

On our [Thankful product page](/thankful) we describe the alternative in plain terms: a kind message, a quiet cup of coffee, something you finally finished. Those are not attempts to reframe the whole day. They are small, specific moments that happened inside it. Thankful gives those moments three spaces, so you do not have to fill a page to make an entry count.

## How do you write in Thankful at night, step by step?

The App Store listing describes Thankful as a quick 3-entry journal that takes just 2 minutes. On a bad day, use those 2 minutes differently from a good day.

1. **Start with a person, not a feeling.** Write who made a small part of the day easier, in one specific sentence: what they said or did, not just their name. Our product page uses this example as an idea for your own journal: "My friend checked in after a long day." If nobody comes to mind, skip this space and come back to it — the spaces are room, not a quota.

2. **Name one small comfort exactly as it was.** A meal you enjoyed, ten quiet minutes with coffee, a shower, a walk around the block. Write what it was and when it happened. A detail from today is what makes a familiar comfort your entry, not a copy of yesterday's.

3. **Write one thing you did, however small.** Started a task you had been putting off, sent the message, got through the meeting, made dinner. On a bad day, "something you did" is often more honest than "something good that happened," because it does not ask you to call the day good.

4. **Read the daily affirmation, then stop.** The affirmation on the Home screen is a pause alongside your journal, not homework and not a test of how positive you can be. Read it, keep any words that feel useful, and close the app. Three short sentences are a complete entry.

5. **Let History hold it without commentary.** The calendar in History lets you revisit an entry by date, and your streak shows the days you returned. Looking back at a bad-day entry a week later is often the point: it shows that a hard day still had specific moments in it, recorded in your own words at the time.

If your problem is not a bad day but the same answers coming back night after night, our earlier guide [What to write in a gratitude journal when you keep repeating yourself](/blog/gratitude-journal-repeating-yourself) walks through how a new detail changes a familiar answer. If you stopped journaling altogether and are returning after a gap, see [How do you restart a gratitude journal after a break?](/blog/thankful-restart-gratitude-journal-after-a-break)

## What should you not force on a bad day?

Do not force gratitude for the thing that hurt. Thankful is a journaling tool, not a substitute for professional care, and you do not need to use gratitude to dismiss a difficult day. Some days the honest first sentence is a hard one, and that sentence belongs in your notes about the day even if it is not one of the three gratitude spaces.

Do not write a polished story. A short, specific sentence is enough to begin, on the product page and in the app. And do not chase the streak: as we put it on the product page, the point of the streak is to make space for your life, not to turn a missed day into another thing to feel bad about. Missing a night and returning the next night is still the practice.

## What do our own numbers say about Thankful so far?

We publish our numbers as measured, even when they are small, and we date them. App Store Connect recorded the following for Thankful in the 28 days from 18 October to 14 November 2026: 444 impressions, 36 product page views, and 2 downloads — one from Japan and one from the United States, both through App Store search. In the most recent 7 days of that window, 8 to 14 November 2026, there were 156 impressions, 6 product page views, and 0 downloads; 69 of those impressions were in the United States, with 4 product page views. These figures come from our App Store Connect measurement dated 15 November 2026 (measured_at 2026-11-15T22:02:59Z).

RevenueCat, in an earlier snapshot on 7 November 2026 for the Thankful project, showed 12 new customers in its trailing 28 days and no active paid subscriptions yet. We do not mix that snapshot date with the App Store Connect window above.

That is the honest picture: a real, published app — version 1.0.3 on the App Store listing we read on 16 November 2026, 18 MB, in Health & Fitness — with a small audience so far. Articles like this one, in the [Thankful hub](/blog/c/thankful), are part of how we grow it: by answering the exact night-time question the app is built for.

## Common questions

### Do I have to write all three things on a bad day?

No. One specific sentence is a complete entry for that night. The three spaces are there when you have three things; on a hard day, filling one honestly is better than forcing three.

### Is it dishonest to write gratitude on a bad day?

No, if you write what was actually true. Naming a person, a small comfort, or something you did does not claim the day was good. It records that those moments were also part of it.

### How long should a night entry take?

The App Store listing describes Thankful as a quick 3-entry journal that takes just 2 minutes. At night, treat that as an upper guide, not a target: stop when you have written something specific.

### Is Thankful free to download?

Yes. Thankful is free to download, with optional Thankful Pro subscriptions as in-app purchases. The App Store listing we read on 16 November 2026 shows Thankful Pro Monthly at $4.99 and Thankful Pro Annual at $39.99. Check the purchase screen in the app for the current offer before you subscribe.

### Which devices does Thankful run on?

Thankful runs on iPhone with iOS 17 or later and iPad with iPadOS 17 or later, as listed on the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/thankful-gratitude-journal/id6759514159). The listing also states that the developer does not collect data from this app.

### Is a gratitude journal a mental-health treatment?

No. Thankful is a journaling tool, not a substitute for professional care. If a day is more than difficult, a journal entry is not the support to rely on alone.

## End the day with one true sentence

You do not need to fix the day before you sleep. Open [Thankful](/thankful), write one specific thing from today in your own words — a person, a small comfort, or something you did — and let the rest wait until tomorrow. [Download Thankful on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/thankful-gratitude-journal/id6759514159) — it is free, and a bad-day entry takes one sentence.
